items.title: Florian J. "Curly" Lizana Interview, 1966-05-18
items.q: The only fellow that I know, and that's the same fellow that I said about playing Napson that I couldn't recall.

ctx.x: Albert. So you must have taken up sax about 1918, 1919, you know, when you were with the jazz ladies at small. Yeah. 1919. Must have been one of the very first ones down here to play sax.

Well, we was. I don't know. The only one fellow that I know, and that's the same fellow that I said about playing Napson that I couldn't recall. I got a picture of him in my mind, but I can't call his name. But he had one of those straight, uh, B-flat, you know, the sax. Soprano. Soprano sax, that's right. Yeah. And, uh, I saw the thing and I saw advantages in it because I could do things with it that I couldn't do with the clarinet. Uh-huh. So I got one of the clarinet and sax, saxophone rather.
Did you get an alto or a tenor or a baritone or bass or soprano first? B-flat, soprano.
